title: Explaining Slow SPN Algebraic-Degree Growth
summary: For one SPN parameter set, the algebraic-degree upper bound rises by 7 per round after round 7; explaining or characterizing this unexpectedly slow growth remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the univariate setting of the studied SPN cipher over $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $w=2$, the upper bound on algebraic degree for parameters $(n,d,h_1,h_2)=(129,1,0,63)$ is reported to grow linearly, increasing by $7$ in every round after round $7$. This behavior is difficult to explain because the comparison quantity $\log_2((2^1+1)\cdot 2^{63})\approx 64.6$ is much larger than $7$. The unresolved problem is to develop a theoretical explanation or characterization of this unexpectedly slow degree growth under these parameter conditions.

scope.domain: Algebraic-degree growth in the univariate setting of the studied SPN cipher over a binary extension field.
parameters: w: fixed to 2 in the studied univariate setting
n, d, h1, h2: fixed to 129, 1, 0, 63 for the parameter instance under study
round number: the reported linear regime increases by 7 per round after round 7
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a theoretical explanation or characterization of the reported unexpectedly slow linear degree growth.
